data.one_liner: Rapier 3D physics backend for flutter_scene using FFI and WebAssembly
data.what_it_does: Implements the abstract physics contract from flutter_scene against the Rapier 3D engine over dart:ffi for native platforms and WebAssembly for the web. Supports rigid bodies, colliders, joints, queries, and collision events.
use_when: You are building 3D games or simulations with flutter_scene
You need 3D rigid body physics, collision detection, and raycasting in Flutter
avoid_when: You are building a 2D game where a 2D physics engine like forge2d is more appropriate
strengths: Supports multiple platforms including Android, iOS, Web, macOS, Linux, and Windows via prebuilt binaries
Includes support for world snapshots and full restoration for rollback prediction
weaknesses: Experimental status means APIs may change between releases
Requires building from source with a Rust toolchain for unsupported targets or when editing native code
data.setup_notes: Requires initializing RapierWorld before use and managing native binaries or web WebAssembly modules.

alternatives.name: forge2d
alternatives.why_pick_it: Pick forge2d if you need 2D physics instead of 3D physics.

alternatives.name: flame
alternatives.why_pick_it: Pick flame if you want a complete 2D game engine rather than just a 3D physics backend for flutter_scene.
